proposal.summary: Area definition (read directly from scratchpad/conv/layers.json): requirement text is "Run bounded research with native identity and complete returned results; supervise owned processes; retain scoped telemetry, failed attempts and recoverable state without granting research workers broker execution authority" -- an agent/process-governance requirement, not primarily an SBOM/CVE/secret-scan requirement. The three recorded winners (grype v0.119.0, syft v1.52.0, gitleaks v8.30.1) still earn their own narrow jobs on reverified evidence (gh api today: all three unarchived, current pins, active within the last 3 days), but none of them was ever evidence for the requirement's actual "no broker execution authority" clause -- that is satisfied today only by a written prompt policy (blueprints/us-equities/workers/policy.md lines 1-4: "do not submit orders, change accounts, read credential stores... Broker credentials belong to a separate execution service") plus the architectural fact that no broker tool is wired into the codex-native-sdk research worker's toolset (catalogs/us-equities/agents-operations.json: "No broker credentials or order tools in the research worker; separate deterministic adapter owns any later approved paper-order work") -- a real but non-technical control that Docker MCP Gateway/Snyk Agent Scan/Cisco AI Defense MCP Scanner all aim at without yet earning a slot. My strongest self-verified finding, beyond the given candidate packet: the catalog's own open_gap "openai-codex 0.154.0 and exchange-calendars 4.13.2 ... have never been Grype-scanned" is true for Grype specifically but misleading about actual coverage -- I opened adoption/sdk/requirements-linux-x86_64-py313.lock myself and found exactly those packages (openai==3.16.2 L565, openai-codex==0.154.0 L571, exchange-calendars==4.13.2 L241), then opened .github/osv-scanner-lockfiles.json (L17) and catalogs/foundation/automation.json and confirmed that exact lock file is already scanned by google/osv-scanner v2.6.0 as a REQUIRED PR check (target_required_checks includes "osv-scanner"). OpenSSF Scorecard is similarly already running in this repo's own CI (scorecard.yml, scheduled) but unreconciled with any layer -- the catalog's own parallel ci-supply-chain layer already flags this exact reconciliation gap verbatim. Gitleaks is genuinely challenged (not yet swapped) by TruffleHog's live provider-API secret verification, confirmed via TruffleHog's own README this session -- a capability class regex/entropy matching cannot produce -- but a credential-safe bounded trial (never real secrets) is needed first, and this repo carries substantial Gitleaks-specific tuning (.gitleaks.toml 26.7K, .gitleaksignore 7.2K) that a switch would need to preserve. Trivy, Cosign and OpenBao each target a distinct, explicitly-named open gap (host-OS/IaC coverage; missing signature/provenance verification; secret lifecycle/leasing) with real primary-source-confirmed capability, but none has run on this stack yet. One researcher citation is corrected here: Cosign's claimed SECURITY.md/"gh attestation verify" precedent is refuted -- sigstore/cosign has no SECURITY.md (404 on contents/SECURITY.md; community-profile security_policy is null) and its actual release process uses ko-sign/a static key, not gh attestation -- this does not weaken Cosign's own directly-confirmed verify capability, only that one supporting claim. Note for the credential-lifecycle framing: broker/API secrets already have an at-rest boundary today (docs/secret-storage.md: per-provider 0600 files outside every worktree, or native Keychain per project memory) -- OpenBao's gap is specifically leasing/rotation/scoping, not "no protection at all." None of these findings move a paper-lane counter (engines run / paper acts passed / paper fills); this is catalog-accuracy and pre-adoption tooling hygiene work, consistent with treating paper-lane results, not catalog activity, as the north-star progress measure.

challengers.trial_plan: No install needed; it already runs. Bounded action: (1) add google/osv-scanner (pin v2.6.0, checksum source https://github.com/google/osv-scanner/releases/download/v2.6.0/osv-scanner_SHA256SUMS) as a recorded component/cross-reference of the security-supply-chain layer in catalogs/landscape/us-equities.json; (2) correct the open_gaps bullets that imply the 36-package SDK has zero vulnerability coverage; (3) pull one real run via `gh run list --workflow=security-scan.yml` and the matching job's logs for a PR that touched adoption/sdk/*, and cite that run ID plus its pass/fail outcome for the SDK lockfile in place of the current zero-citation gap language. Pass criterion: the corrected catalog entry cites a specific, verifiable CI run covering that lockfile. Overturn condition: if that run history shows the scanner silently skips adoption/sdk/* despite being listed (parser failure), the original gap claim stands and no correction should be made.

challengers.name: TruffleHog
challengers.why_better: Fetched its own README directly this session: 'For every potential credential that is detected, we've painstakingly implemented programmatic verification against the API that we think it belongs to,' with 'over 700 credential detectors that support active verification' and 'over 800 secret types' classified. This is a structural capability -- live true/false verification against the credential's own provider -- that Gitleaks' regex/entropy matching cannot produce at any version, and it directly closes the layer's own stated gap that the 2026-09-19 Gitleaks receipt 'does not certify that no secrets exist.' Repo metadata reconfirmed today: v3.97.9 released 2026-09-24, pushed TODAY (2026-09-26T15:19:54Z), 28,061 stars, AGPL-3.0, unarchived.
challengers.trial_plan: This project's own prior review correctly flagged that live-verification cannot ethically be exercised against real secrets in a read-only session. Resolve it the way the existing Grype receipt already validates true-positive detection with a deliberately-vulnerable positive-control fixture: (1) run `trufflehog git "$PROJECT_ROOT" --no-verification` (verification off) over the same 22-commit range the 2026-09-19 Gitleaks receipt covers, as a pattern-detection-only, zero-outbound-call comparison; (2) separately run it against one syntactically-valid but already-revoked/placeholder test string (never a real key) to confirm it reports 'unverified/inactive' and never manufactures a false live-positive. Pass criterion: matches or exceeds Gitleaks' 0-true-positive result on the same range, with the placeholder case confirming honest verification semantics. Overturn condition: if `--no-verification` mode loses meaningful detector coverage versus Gitleaks' tuned .gitleaks.toml rules, or AGPL-3.0 turns out to require any code linkage (run only as a separate CLI process, per the candidate's own correct license caveat).

researched_candidates.fit: The one candidate this round that targets the layer's ACTUAL requirement text head-on -- 'supervise owned processes ... without granting research workers broker execution authority' -- rather than the narrower SBOM/vuln/secret-scanning reading the three adopted winners address; every MCP tool call in a stack like this one (ai-memory, codebase-memory, qmd, serena, jcodemunch, etc.) is exactly the 'research worker' action the requirement wants bounded, and a gateway that scopes secrets/egress per-MCP-server is a structural mechanism for that where Grype/Syft/Gitleaks are silent. Two close 2025-2026 alternatives, both independently confirmed via gh api, worth naming alongside it: (1) Snyk Agent Scan (https://github.com/snyk/agent-scan) -- Invariant Labs, its original author, was acquired by Snyk in June 2025 (snyk.io/news, corroborated by GlobeNewswire/Techzine/Yahoo Finance), and 'gh api repos/invariantlabs-ai/mcp-scan' now silently redirects to snyk/agent-scan (v0.6.4, released 2026-09-21, pushed TODAY 2026-09-26T12:21:47Z, 3,091 stars, Apache-2.0) -- a rename/ownership change a naive stars-or-awesome-list snapshot would misattribute to a dead repo; it is a pre-install scanner (prompt injection/tool-poisoning/destructive-capability detection), not a runtime gate. (2) Cisco AI Defense MCP Scanner (cisco-ai-defense/mcp-scanner, tag 4.8.4, released 2026-08-28, pushed 2026-09-19, 1,079 stars, Apache-2.0) -- YARA + LLM-based + behavioral pre-install scanning with explicit supply-chain checks. None of the three has any native_execution evidence on this stack; all are unarchived and actively pushed within the last week. Docker's own repo has no GitHub Releases API entries (ships via CLI-plugin/Docker Desktop channel) but carries proper semver git tags, latest v0.44.1 (tag commit dated 2026-09-16), 1,587 stars, MIT, pushed 2026-09-23.
